name: Target
description: Target is a general-merchandise retailer with 1,995 stores across the US and a digital storefront; nearly all online orders are fulfilled from stores. It sells food and everyday essentials, beauty, apparel, home goods and toys and electronics, mostly its own and national brands, plus shop-in-shops with Apple, Levi's and Ulta Beauty and Starbucks cafes. Money comes from the margin between what it pays vendors and shelf prices on $102.7B of merchandise, plus fast-growing advertising (Roundel, $915M), credit-card profit sharing and other income. Fiscal 2025 sales fell 1.7 percent and operating income fell 8.1 percent; Michael Fiddelke became CEO in February 2026.

businessLines.name: Food & beverage
businessLines.how: Resale markup on groceries and prepared items bought from suppliers and sold to shoppers per visit; low margin but drives frequent store traffic.
businessLines.description: Dry and perishable grocery, snacks, candy, beverages, deli, bakery, meat, produce, food service (primarily Starbucks) and floral.

revenue.note: vs $23,828M FY2024 (+1.3%); Target reports one segment and no profit by category

businessLines.name: Household essentials
businessLines.how: Resale markup on everyday consumables bought repeatedly; low margin but steady traffic.
businessLines.description: Includes household cleaning, paper products, over-the-counter healthcare, vitamins and supplements, baby gear and pet supplies (10-K note f).

businessLines.name: Hardlines
businessLines.how: Resale markup on discretionary goods; higher margin than food but more sensitive to consumer spending and holiday timing.
businessLines.description: Includes electronics (video games and consoles), toys, sporting goods, entertainment and luggage (10-K note d); being remade as 'Fun 101'.

businessLines.name: Apparel & accessories
businessLines.how: Sales of owned-brand and national-brand clothing and accessories at a markup; seasonal and markdown-driven.

businessLines.name: Home furnishings & decor
businessLines.how: Markup on furniture, decor and seasonal goods; the weakest-trending category.
businessLines.description: Includes bed and bath, decor, school and office supplies, storage, small appliances, kitchenware, furniture, lighting, home improvement and seasonal (10-K note e).

businessLines.name: Beauty
businessLines.how: Markup on beauty and personal-care products sold in stores and online, including Ulta Beauty at Target shops.

revenue.note: vs $13,173M FY2024; $12,538M FY2023; includes Ulta Beauty at Target shop-in-shops

businessLines.name: Advertising revenue (Roundel)
businessLines.how: Vendors and brands pay Target to place ads on its site, app and in stores; no cost of goods, so margin is far above merchandise.

businessLines.name: Credit card profit sharing and other revenue
businessLines.how: Target receives a share of profit on its branded credit cards, plus other income lines; not itemised further in the 10-K read.
